title: Church Ordinances
definition: Church ordinances are the practices commanded by Christ for His Church, especially baptism and the Lord's Supper.
summary: The ordinances visibly proclaim the Gospel and mark faithful obedience to Christ.
christFocus: Christ gave baptism and the Lord's Supper to His Church as visible signs that point to His saving work and His gathered people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church ordinances are commanded practices given by Christ to His people. Baptism and the Lord's Supper are not human inventions or empty traditions; they are visible Gospel signs that teach, remind, and confess.

Baptism marks identification with Christ and entrance into visible discipleship. The Lord's Supper remembers Christ's death and proclaims His sacrifice until He comes.

The ordinances do not replace faith in Christ. They point to Christ and call the Church to obedience, worship, unity, and Gospel clarity.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without ordinances, the Church loses visible Gospel reminders Christ gave for its life and witness. This doctrine matters because it guards the Church from treating commanded practices as optional or meaningless.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor the ordinances with reverence and biblical understanding. Participate in them as acts of obedience and Gospel remembrance, not as mere religious routine.
